_note: Grade 2 vowels, round 3 (English literacy year, Part 12.3; types/_shared/vowels-g2b.js; written by s-g2vow/round3/bank-b.js). `read`: the reading pages of the lessons oo/ou/ow/oi/oy (G2-543), ar and or (G2-544), er, ir, and ur (G2-545): per lesson the spellings (the frozen word lists of G2-532..534), the spellings each level reads, the examples of the page instruction, words never printed in a text (`avoid`), yes-or-no sentences, riddles (an answer and the list words that answer it too), the words that fill a riddle box (they answer no riddle), and read-and-draw sentences. `syll`: two-syllable words with a long vowel by level (compound words with a vowel team, a silent e, an open first syllable): the two parts and the syllables with a long vowel; sentences to choose a word from three (G2-546); yes-or-no sentences (G2-547); `joins`: every first part and second part of a level that make a real word. `heart`: the heart words could, would, should and their companions with their sound boxes and hearts (from the Heart Words tool), and sentences whose missing word is named by its first letter (G2-548).

words.note: oul says /oo/ and the l is silent
the would, could, should family all share oul
e says /i/ or /uh/ (not its name), au says /u/ here (not /aw/), and se says /z/: each can be defended as a tricky part, so the key hearts all three (review en-1119-lit, 2026-11-19)
ie says /e/ — there is an i hiding in friend
the a says /e/, like in many
the a says /e/ — many does not rhyme with canny
eo says /ee/ — the o is along for the ride
oe says /u/ — the s saying /z/ is an ordinary rule, not the heart
the o says /u/ right at the start
